newsitem.title: UK: UK power watchdog proposes National Grid price cut.
newsitem.headline: UK power watchdog proposes National Grid price cut.

text.p: Britain's power industry watchdog on Thursday proposed a one-off cut in National Grid Group Plc's transmission price controls of 20 percent followed by RPI-4 in each of the following three years.
OFFER head Stephen Littlechild said in a statement that the new controls should mean benefits to customers of one billion stg over the period.
Speaking on BBC Radio news, Littlechild said domestic customers should see cuts in their bills of four stg a year and larger decreases for bigger customers.
"It is a tough proposal but a realistic one," he said.
OFFER's initial range for the one-off price cuts had been between 20 and 26 percent, with future levels at RPI-4.
Littlechild said he had listened to National Grid's representations on those proposals and made some modifications.
He said that if National Grid did not find the latest plans acceptable, he would expect the issue to be referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.

In a statement, OFFER said National Grid stood to gain or lose up to 21 million stg in 1997/98 depending on its success in responding to incentives on transport uplift, reactive power and transmission losses.

OFFER said the calculations for the latest plans were based on cost of capital of seven percent and an initial asset valuation of 4.15 billion stg, which is 150 million stg above the figure assumed in previous proposals. OFFER said calculations were also based on controllable operating costs reducing at four percent a year in real terms.
If National Grid accepts the latest plans, the new price control would become effective from April 1, 1997.
